# Computer Networks
Computers talk to each other over data cable. A network is everything joined by cable, switches and routers; a router gives every computer on it an address, and connects it to the other networks.
## Wiring it up - [bold]Data cable[/bold] is laid like power cable, and joins the machines along it. - A [bold]network switch[/bold] joins the cable on its tile and the four tiles beside it, and any switch or router next to it, into one network, while it has power. - A [bold]network router[/bold] does the same, and also gives every computer on its network an address, connects its network to the others, and keeps the list of hostnames. - A [bold]network firewall[/bold] is a switch that, in cyberspace, shuts the way past it to netrunners its ID reader doesn't pass. Rack it beside the router and cable the machines it guards to it alone.
Without a powered router, cabled computers have no address and can't send anything.
## Addresses and hostnames - [mono]ip[/mono] shows a computer's address, like [mono]10.1.1.2[/mono]. A computer keeps its address while it stays on the network, but may get a different one if it is unplugged. - [mono]hostname door-console[/mono] names a computer. Names are 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and -, and are kept through reboots. The terminal window's title shows the computer's hostname and address. - [mono]hosts[/mono] lists every name the routers know.
Since addresses can change, programs should find each other by name.
## Sending packets In Wire, the [bold]net[/bold] module sends and receives: - [mono]net.send(host, port, text)[/mono] sends up to 1024 bytes to an address or a hostname, on a port from 0 to 65535. It arrives the next tick. - [mono]net.receive()[/mono] returns the packets that have arrived, each with [mono].sender[/mono], [mono].port[/mono] and [mono].text[/mono]. - [mono]net.neighbours()[/mono] lists the other machines on the same network.
The examples folder has [mono]ping.wire[/mono], [mono]echo_server.wire[/mono] and [mono]netscan.wire[/mono] to start from.
## Working other machines Any machine people work through a window, like a vending machine or a console, joins the network when it stands on data cable, and gets an address of its own. A program on a computer can work it as if someone stood at it, with the [bold]dev[/bold] module: - [mono]dev.info(host)[/mono] says what the machine is, and the calls it takes with their arguments. - [mono]dev.state(host)[/mono] reads what its window shows. - [mono]dev.call(host, call, args)[/mono] does what pressing something in its window does, like [mono]dev.call(host, "vending_machine_eject", {"type": "Regular", "id": "DrinkColaCan"})[/mono].
The computer has no ID of its own, so a machine that needs access turns it away, and a machine without power doesn't answer. [mono]examples/machines.wire[/mono] lists the machines on a network and their calls; [mono]man dev[/mono] has the rest.
